course_description:
More advanced reading, translation and composition based on up-to-date specimens of modern Chinese.

This is an advanced-level course in written Chinese that carries on from CHIN3200 and aims to further develop students' literacy skills in Modern Chinese. The instruction covers three aspects of language use. First, we will focus on reading and writing two genres: argumentation and narration. Argumentation is about truth, logic, and evidence. Narration is about structuring lived experience in time and space. Both genres are fundamental to the development of literacy skills. Secondly, we will explore different registers such that writing to a customer at a workplace setting is different from messaging close friends. Finally, new words and grammatical structures are introduced based on various advanced topics, such as Confucianism and migrant workers in contemporary China.

course_aims: Building on the content of CHIN3200, this course aims to furtherﾠdevelop students' skills in reading and writing Modern Standard Chinese in representative styles in different topicsﾠand to develop basic skills in translating from Chinese into English. Students are guided through a graded series of Chinese materials of various genres, including short stories, fiction, essays, and newspaper articles.

learning_outcomes.description: Read and translate into English general authentic texts in Modern Standard Chinese with the aid of a dictionary.
Read both simplified and traditional Chinese characters at the advanced level.
Improve general writing skills in Chinese to the advanced level or above.
Gain better knowledge and understanding of Chinese language.
Demonstrate respect for cultural and social diversity and for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples and perspectives.
Demonstrate knowledge and respect for ethics and ethical standards in completing assessment tasks.
Lead self and others in group activities.
Be confident dealing with ambiguity and uncertainty.
Present persuasive oral and written arguments.
Be empathetic of other people, cultures, and knowledge systems.

assessment_details.other_conditions: Time limited, Secure. See the conditions definitions
assessment_details.task_description: In-class exam on L6, L7, L8 and other materials covered in class. The exam is comprised of two tasks: character writing and essay writing. The character writing focuses on words learned from each lesson. The essay writing focuses on using the rhetorical styles and other writing skills we have discussed in class. This assessment task is designed to enhance students’ ability to communicate with cultural sensitivity and engage thoughtfully in discussions on key issues relevant to both Australian and Chinese workplace contexts. Intercultural (Australia vs. China) and intracultural (indigenous perspectives) examples will be discussed and provided in class to help students prepare for the assessment. Check Blackboard for the marking rubric. AI and MT Statement This assessment task is to be completed in-person. The use of generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) or Machine Translation (MT) tools will not be permitted. assessment_details.other_conditions: Time limited, Secure. See the conditions definitions
assessment_details.task_description: Time & Date: 3:00 pm – 5:00 pm, Tuesday, November 10, 2026 Venue: 32-415 Assessment Note: Please be aware that the entire interview will be audio/video recorded for assessment and marking purposes. The entire interview consists of two main parts and will take approximately 12 minutes to complete. At the start, you will be handed two paragraphs selected directly from the main texts of the lessons covered after the mid-semester exam. You will have exactly 5 minutes of quiet time to read through these paragraphs and organize your thoughts. Please note that cell phones and dictionaries are not permitted for translation; however, you may use a pen or pencil to take notes or mark the text directly. Following your preparation time, you will begin the 7-minute interactive session by providing a concise summary of the paragraphs. The interviewer will then ask a series of questions based on the text. These will include direct questions to verify your understanding of specific details, as well as conceptual, open-ended, and follow-up questions that allow you to expand on the themes, express your opinions, or connect the reading to broader topics discussed in class. You may refer to your notes or the paragraphs throughout the interview without penalty. Check Blackboard for the marking rubric. AI and MT Statement This assessment task is to be completed in-person.
